claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy will provide superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance at elevated temperature compared with conventional structural alloys.
The multi-principal-element composition of AlCoCrFeNi promotes formation of a robust oxide layer.
The oxide layer formed on AlCoCrFeNi is self-healing.
The oxide layer mitigates both wear and corrosion.
Simultaneous sliding and corrosive exposure at 500–600°C will produce a stable, adherent oxide or passive film on the AlCoCrFeNi surface.
Synergy among the multiple principal elements promotes efficient passivation of AlCoCrFeNi.
At elevated temperature, the oxide film reduces the initiation of corrosion pits.
At elevated temperature, the oxide film reduces removal of wear particles.
Reduced pit initiation and wear-particle removal slow overall tribo-corrosion degradation.
AlCoCrFeNi will exhibit lower mass loss than a conventional structural alloy under the same test conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will exhibit smaller wear scars than a conventional structural alloy under the same test conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will exhibit fewer corrosion pits than a conventional structural alloy under the same test conditions.
Processing conditions and microstructural heterogeneity may limit the proposed degradation-resistance benefit.
Chemical or temperature extremes beyond the proposed test range may destabilize the oxide film.
The magnitude of improvement may vary with processing method and environmental conditions.
